<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of
                      <jats:italic>Rhus chinensis</jats:italic>
                      in complex mountainous field conditions.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Experimental results showed that the proposed model for flower detection achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 89.5 and an inference speed of 56 frames per second (FPS). After applying acceleration strategies during model deployment on the edge computing device, the processing throughput reached 192 FPS with a mAP of 89.2; a 3.1% increase in mAP and approximately a 5.6 times improvement in FPS compared to the original YOLOv5s.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results demonstrate that the proposed lightweight model and acceleration strategies effectively balance high accuracy with high-throughput onboard image processing. The developed UAV-edge computing system provides a promising prototype for future efficient nectar flowering status monitoring, with potential applications in smart apiculture.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    We introduceMonkeyOCR, a document parsing model that advances the state of the art by leveraging a structure-recognition-relation (SRR) triplet paradigm. This design simplifies what would otherwise be a complex multi-tool pipeline and avoids the inefficiencies of processing full pages with giant end-to-end models. In SRR, document parsing is abstracted into three fundamental questions—“Where is it?” (structure), “What is it?” (recognition), and “How is it organized?” (relation)—corresponding to structure detection, content recognition, and relation prediction. To support this paradigm, we present MonkeyDoc, a comprehensive dataset with 4.5 million bilingual instances spanning over ten document types, which addresses the limitations of existing datasets that often focus on a single task, language, or document type. Leveraging the SRR paradigm and MonkeyDoc, we trained a 3B-parameter document foundation model. We further identify parameter redundancy in this model and propose contiguous parameter degradation (CPD), enabling the construction of models from 0.6B to 1.2B parameters that run faster with an acceptable performance drop. MonkeyOCR achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing previous open-source and closed-source methods, including Gemini 2.5 Pro. Additionally, the model can be efficiently deployed for inference on a single RTX 3090 GPU. Code and models will be released at

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Flexible wearable sensors have transformed motion tracking, soft robotics, and human-machine interfaces by enabling precise movement detection and adaptability to curved surfaces. However, conventional composite sensors often face challenges such as limited sensitivity, detection range, linearity, and durability. In this study, we propose a stretchable auxetic sensing textile with a negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR) structure, incorporating reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and carbon nanotubes (CNT) by micro-crack engineering to enhance its mechanical durability and sensing performance. Integrating macro-scale NPR with micro-scale wrinkles, this innovative design achieves a high sensitivity of 11.2 within a wide detection range (0–100%), a more linear sensing range with an
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    value of 0.998, an ultra-low detection limit of 0.5%, and exceptional durability, outperforming conventional wearable sensors. Additionally, the textile sensor boasts excellent moisture permeability (32.7 g m
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    h
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) and a remarkable NPR value of −0.25, ensuring comfort and adaptability for various wearable applications. Integrated with deep learning algorithms, the auxetic sensing textile demonstrates 98% accuracy in recognizing soft robotic movements at various bending angles. It is capable of capturing both smallscale physiological signals, such as electrocardiograms, and large-scale movements, offering significant freedom of movement and adaptability to complex surfaces.
                  </jats:p>
